Night trains return to Europe

By Ada Example

After years of decline, overnight rail services are coming back across Europe. Operators are ordering new sleeper cars, and several capitals are linked again by trains that leave after dinner and arrive before breakfast.

The revival has several causes. Travellers want to avoid short flights, cities are keen on direct links, and new rolling stock makes the journeys more comfortable than the aging couchettes many passengers remember.

What changed

Timetables were redesigned so that trains pass through busy junctions at night, when tracks are free. Ticket prices dropped on some routes because several operators now share the same carriages.

  • Vienna to Amsterdam, three times a week
  • Berlin to Brussels, every night in summer

Critics point out that capacity is still small. A single sleeper train carries a few hundred people, while a day train on the same line can carry more than a thousand. The operators answer that the night market is different and growing.
Ticket sales rose again last year.
